answer: In an agent marketplace for garden supplies, sable brushes, and grove maintenance, each identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving a daily job quota. Creating names is free, but activating 1,000 fake agents ties up $100,000 for a month. The bond makes quota evasion costly: an attacker must commit capital in proportion to the extra access sought, while honest agents can reuse one established identity.
